strategies.title: [local-likelihood-correction] Replace the misspecified binomial decoder
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: local-likelihood-correction  
Replacement scope: Replace only the `EDGE_COUNT` query decoding block beginning at `// Decode by maximizing the exact binomial likelihood...`; keep the current graph construction and strategy-selection logic unchanged.  
Compute budget: none; O(M) arithmetic per query, strictly less work than the present logarithmic likelihood calculation.  
Gain mechanism: The current decoder models the noisy total edge count as `Binomial(L,p)` with candidate-dependent variance `L p(1-p)`. That is not the actual channel: for a source graph with `e` edges, the observed total is `Binomial(e,1-epsilon)+Binomial(L-e,epsilon)`, whose mean is `epsilon L+(1-2epsilon)e` and whose variance is exactly `L epsilon(1-epsilon)`, independent of `e`. Thus the present decoder systematically overweights extreme-density graphs by incorrectly assigning them lower variance.  

For `0<epsilon<0.5`, decode to the candidate whose expected observed count
`mu_j=epsilon*L+(1-2*epsilon)*edge_count[j]`
is closest to the received edge count; ties use the smaller index. This is the maximum-likelihood rule under the normal approximation with the correct common variance and is also the correct midpoint decision rule for the exact symmetric scalar channel except for small lattice corrections. For `epsilon=0`, the same rule reduces exactly to nearest original edge count. Preserve graph validity because no output construction changes: all strings remain length `L`, all counts remain in `[0,L]`, and `4<=N<=100` is unchanged.  
Expected-gain check: this introduces the corrected common-variance decision boundary, which the incumbent’s candidate-dependent-variance likelihood cannot realize; accept this strategy only if the 50-case `combined_score` exceeds the incumbent threshold `13,844,806.2`.

strategies.title: [mesoscopic-channel-design] Select N by predicted roulette-score survival rather
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: mesoscopic-channel-design  
Replacement scope: Replace the block computing `L_ideal`, `N_candidate_EC`, and the EDGE_COUNT branch’s chosen `N_ACTUAL`; retain the small-N GED construction and retain equally spaced edge-count codewords for the edge-count branch.  
Compute budget: no optimizer starts; evaluate all 97 legal values `N=4..100`, with O(97M) Gaussian-CDF operations once before graph output; query time is unchanged.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent chooses `N` from a hand-set `K_SEP=2.5` spacing rule, but the stated score is not a raw classification-rate objective: with independent queries and per-query success probability `p`, its expected unrounded score is proportional to
`(0.9+0.1p)^100/N`.
This explicitly prices both the severe 100-query error multiplier and graph size. For each candidate `N`, let `L=N(N-1)/2`, use the existing rounded equally spaced source counts `e_j`, set means `mu_j=epsilon*L+(1-2epsilon)*e_j`, and place decision boundaries halfway between adjacent means. With `sigma=sqrt(L*epsilon*(1-epsilon))`, calculate each source’s predicted correct probability from normal CDF differences between its two boundaries, average them to obtain `p`, and maximize `(0.9+0.1p)^100/N`. At epsilon zero, use the exact rule: choose the smallest N for which all M integer counts can be distinct, giving predicted `p=1`. Use the selected N only when it exceeds the applicable GED size, preserving the incumbent’s strong small-isomorphism regime. All hard constraints remain automatic because the search enumerates only legal N and all codeword counts are clamped to `[0,L]`.  
Expected-gain check: the selected N maximizes the explicit approximation `(0.9+0.1p)^100/N` over every legal edge-count construction size whereas the incumbent evaluates only one `K_SEP`-derived size; the falsifiable threshold is a 50-case `combined_score` above `13,844,806.2`.

strategies.title: [structural-degree-code] Replace scalar density codewords with clique-partition
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: structural-degree-code  
Replacement scope: Replace the entire large-N `EDGE_COUNT` graph-generation phase and its query decoder; leave the GED branch untouched.  
Compute budget: no randomized starts; construct at most M deterministic partitions, and decode each query in O(MN log N) after sorting degrees. This is below the current worst-case interactive budget for `N<=100`, `M<=100`, and 100 queries.  
Gain mechanism: Edge-count encoding discards all invariant information except one scalar. Instead, use graphs that are disjoint unions of cliques, with codeword `k` represented by a deterministic partition of N into clique sizes. Enumerate partitions through a mixed-radix composition: reserve `B=floor(sqrt(N))` vertices for a “fine” clique-size channel and distribute the remaining vertices among `q` equal-sized cliques plus one residual clique, producing M distinct sorted degree multisets. Decode by sorting received degrees and comparing against each candidate’s expected noisy degree multiset:
`epsilon*(N-1)+(1-2epsilon)*d_v`,
using squared error normalized by `N*epsilon*(1-epsilon)*(N-1)`, with total-edge-count midpoint distance as a deterministic tie-breaker. Vertex shuffling is removed by sorting, while the degree histogram supplies many correlated but genuinely additional invariant observations unavailable to the incumbent’s scalar count. Generate every graph directly from clique membership, so each output remains a valid simple undirected N-vertex graph of exactly length `N(N-1)/2`.  
Expected-gain check: unlike the incumbent, this construction can separate two candidates having similar total edge counts by different multiplicities of noisy degree modes; the falsifiable evaluator threshold is a 50-case `combined_score` above `13,844,806.2`.

strategies.title: [covariance-profile-decoder] Replace the double-counted degree/edge decoder with
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: covariance-profile-decoder

Replacement scope: Replace only the `Strategy::EDGE_COUNT` query-decoding block beginning at `const std::vector<int> observed = sorted_degrees_from_string(...)` through selection of `best_g_idx`; retain the current clique-partition encoder and its selected codewords.

Compute budget: none; O(MN) arithmetic per query, with no new optimizer starts or iterations. Evaluation-time effect is negligible and slightly faster because it removes per-candidate edge-variance calculation.

Gain mechanism: The present score adds squared degree residuals and then separately adds an edge-count residual, although the total degree is exactly twice the edge count. Thus it double-counts one noisy direction and uses the wrong covariance geometry. Under independent edge flips, degrees have variance `(N-1)ε(1-ε)` and every pair of distinct degrees has covariance `ε(1-ε)`. For each sorted candidate expected degree profile, score the residual vector `d` by the equicorrelated Gaussian inverse covariance:
`(||d||²-(sum d)²/N)/((N-2)a) + (sum d)²/(2N(N-1)a)`, where `a=ε(1-ε)`, with ordinary exact matching when `ε=0`.

This preserves all validity constraints because graph generation and N remain unchanged; only the predicted index changes. It also has an incumbent fallback: retain the existing score for numerical handling only when `N<=2`, which never occurs legally.

Expected-gain check: this introduces a likelihood direction unavailable to the incumbent—separating degree-shape noise from the total-degree mode rather than counting that mode twice—and is falsifiably worthwhile only if the evaluator exceeds the incumbent combined score 15454224.56.

strategies.title: [complemented-partition-codebook] Expand clique partitions into a complement-pai
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: complemented-partition-codebook

Replacement scope: Replace `build_clique_partition_codewords`, including its truncated lexicographic partition enumeration and its codeword-selection phase, while keeping the large-N degree-based query interface.

Compute budget: generate at most 4096 integer partitions/candidate structures, expand each into at most two graphs, and perform incremental farthest-first selection for at most 100 codewords. Hard bound: at most 8192 candidates and at most `8192*100*N` degree-distance operations. Query cost remains O(MN).

Gain mechanism: Every selected union-of-cliques codeword should be accompanied by its graph complement, i.e. a complete multipartite graph with the same part sizes. These are geometrically distinct graphs: clique codes create high within-block correlations and sparse between-block contact, while complements create the reverse topology. Their degree profiles transform from `s-1` to `N-s`, and their edge densities also move to `L-E`. Selecting jointly from both families gives the farthest-first stage access to low-, middle-, and high-density degree signatures rather than relying on the first 4096 partitions reached by a recursion that is biased toward large early parts.

Represent candidates as `(sorted block sizes, complement_bit)`. For each candidate, calculate its sorted degree vector, edge count, and emitted adjacency string directly. Seed farthest-first with the empty graph and complete graph; then maintain each candidate’s nearest selected distance incrementally using `sum_v(degA[v]-degB[v])² + 2*abs(edgesA-edgesB)`. Decode using the calibrated covariance-profile score from the local strategy.

All generated graphs are legal N-vertex undirected graphs, since each emitted bit is deterministically computed from “same block” XOR `complement_bit`; N remains in `[4,100]`.

Expected-gain check: the incumbent cannot select a complete-multipartite complement unless that graph accidentally appears as a different clique partition, which is generally impossible beyond trivial cases; the explicit new complement topology is falsifiably beneficial only if combined score exceeds 15454224.56.

strategies.title: [threshold-graph-codebook] Replace disconnected-clique coding by nested-neighbor
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: threshold-graph-codebook

Replacement scope: Replace the complete large-N construction phase—`build_clique_partition_codewords` and its stored clique degree vectors—with threshold-graph candidate generation, maximin codeword selection, and corresponding stored expected degree profiles. Replace the large-N decoder with the covariance-profile decoder.

Compute budget: candidate pool is capped at 4096 creation strings plus their complements, maximum 8192 candidates. Generate candidates deterministically from all creation strings when `N<=13`, otherwise from 4096 fixed-seed Bernoulli creation strings spanning probabilities `0/32,1/32,...,32/32`; incremental farthest-first uses at most `8192*100*N` primitive operations. Query time remains O(MN), with no graph-isomorphism work.

Gain mechanism: A threshold graph is generated by starting with vertex 0 and repeatedly adding either an isolated vertex (`0`) or a dominating vertex (`1`) connected to all earlier vertices. Unlike a union of cliques, it has a nested, non-disconnected neighborhood topology and exponentially many realizable degree profiles. Its creation string directly supplies diverse monotone degree spectra; taking complements additionally reverses contact topology. Select M strings by farthest-first separation in expected sorted degree profile plus edge count, then emit the graph from the creation rule. This escapes the limited integer-partition manifold, whose count and shape diversity constrain the incumbent.

For a creation string `b[1..N-1]`, append vertex `j`; edge `(i,j)` exists exactly when `b[j]=1`. Compute degrees by summing those emitted edges, sort them, and decode from sorted observed degrees. The construction always emits exactly `N(N-1)/2` bits and respects all N bounds. Use the present GED implementation unchanged for small-M cases where it is selected.

Expected-gain check: threshold creation strings add an exponential nested-neighborhood degree-spectrum family that no disjoint-clique partition can realize; this structural escape is falsifiably accepted only if it beats combined score 15454224.56.

strategies.title: [profile-aware-codebook-selection] Noise-whitened farthest-first selection over
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: profile-aware-codebook-selection

Replacement scope: Replace only the candidate-to-candidate `distance` lambda and the farthest-first selection phase inside `build_complement_partition_codewords`; retain the existing partition enumeration, clique/complement graph construction, output representation, selected-code storage, and query decoder.

Compute budget: none beyond the current `O(C^2 N)` farthest-first work; maintain a cached candidate-feature vector and update each candidate’s nearest selected distance incrementally. Expected evaluation-time effect: negligible to slightly lower, because the currently computed edge-count absolute-difference term can be replaced by cached feature arithmetic.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent selects candidates using `sum squared sorted-degree differences + 2*abs(edge difference)`, but decodes using noisy degrees and a correlated edge-count observation. Replace this surrogate with the Gaussian channel geometry induced by independent edge flips. For two candidates with sorted degree profiles `d,e`, define `x_v=(1-2ε)(d_v-e_v)`. The degree-noise covariance is exactly `ε(1-ε)((N-2)I+J)`, since any two distinct vertex degrees share exactly their common edge-noise variable. Use the resulting Mahalanobis separation
`Ddeg = [sum x_v^2 - (sum x_v)^2/(2N-2)] / (ε(1-ε)(N-2))`
for `N>2`, and append one independent residual feature based on edge count after removing the degree-sum component. Concretely, use the two-dimensional feature `(sorted degrees, total edges)` but give the edge residual zero weight because total degree already determines total edges exactly; this prevents the incumbent’s double-counted and dimensionally inconsistent `2*abs(edge difference)` term from steering selection toward density-only codewords. For `ε=0`, use the limiting deterministic metric `sum(d_v-e_v)^2`, with a lexicographic tie break on edge difference. Farthest-first then directly maximizes a separation aligned with the actual degree decoder rather than the old hand-weighted structural proxy.

All generated candidates remain unions of cliques or their complements on exactly `N` vertices, so every emitted string remains a valid length-`N(N-1)/2` undirected graph encoding and `4<=N<=100` remains unchanged. Expected-gain check: this introduces the covariance-corrected separation direction that the incumbent selector cannot express through `sum delta² + 2|ΔE|`; accept it only if the evaluator reports combined_score strictly above `17358828.78`.

strategies.title: [biclique-component-channel] Replace clique partitions by disjoint complete-bipa
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: biclique-component-channel

Replacement scope: Replace `build_complement_partition_codewords` completely for the large-`N` branch, including its partition candidate enumeration and graph materialization; retain the current `N` selection, graph-string output arrays, degree-based query path, and small-graph GED branch.

Compute budget: enumerate at most 4096 canonical multisets of unordered component pairs `(a,b)` with `a>=b>=1`, whose total vertex count is `N`; materialize both each union-of-bicliques graph and its complement, giving at most 8192 candidates. Use one deterministic incremental farthest-first pass, no optimizer starts and no iterations. Expected evaluation-time effect: comparable to the incumbent partition codebook, with `O(8192*M*N)` feature selection and only `O(MN²)` graph output construction.

Gain mechanism: A clique component of size `s` contributes `s` vertices of degree `s-1`; its complement contributes only the globally inverted version of that block structure. A complete bipartite component `K_{a,b}` instead contributes `a` vertices of degree `b` and `b` vertices of degree `a`, independently controlling multiplicities and degree levels. Thus it realizes degree multisets such as repeated low/high paired levels that cannot be produced by any disjoint clique partition or its complement. Enumerate component pairs in non-increasing canonical order: recursively choose `(a,b)` with `a>=b`, require each next pair to be lexicographically no larger than the previous pair, and stop when the remaining vertex budget reaches zero. For every decomposition, construct edges exactly between the two sides of each component and nowhere else; also construct its complement. Compute sorted degrees and edge counts, then select `M` candidates by farthest-first distance in the covariance-aware degree metric from the first strategy, seeded by empty, complete, and the candidate nearest half density if available. Decode with the unchanged sorted-degree likelihood, because vertex shuffling preserves this invariant.

The construction is deterministic, uses all `N` vertices exactly once, produces symmetric simple graphs with no self-loops, and emits the required triangular bit strings. Expected-gain check: the biclique-side multiplicity degree profiles are a strict structural superset in a direction unavailable to clique/complement partitions, so retain the replacement only if its measured combined_score exceeds `17358828.78`.

strategies.title: [cograph-cotree-exploration] Alternating join/union cotree codebook with exact d
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: cograph-cotree-exploration

Replacement scope: Replace the large-`N` codeword construction and candidate enumeration phase, rather than augmenting `build_complement_partition_codewords`; retain the common output arrays and replace only the large-branch decoder’s expected-profile source with the cotree candidate degree profiles.

Compute budget: generate at most 2048 deterministic cotree candidates and their complements, no random starts and no iterative optimization. Build each candidate in `O(N²)`, calculate degree multisets in `O(N²)`, and perform incremental farthest-first selection in `O(4096*M*N)`. Expected evaluation-time effect: bounded below roughly 0.2 seconds in C++ for `N<=100`, excluding the unchanged interactive I/O.

Gain mechanism: Explore the larger cograph topology rather than merely disconnected cliques and their complements. A cograph cotree recursively combines vertex modules using either disjoint union or complete join. Build deterministic candidates from integer leaf-size partitions by alternating operations by depth: start with leaf independent sets of selected sizes, pair adjacent modules, then alternate union and join at each merge level; cyclically rotate the leaf-size partition before merging to create distinct module contacts. Also include the complement of each cotree. Unlike clique partitions, this permits nested module joins: for example, a joined pair of internally disconnected modules followed by union with a joined module creates three independently repeated degree bands with selectively complete cross-band contacts. Those band contacts alter degree multiplicities without requiring the global inversion forced by the incumbent complement option. Canonicalize each candidate by its sorted degree multiset plus edge count, discard exact duplicate graph strings, and select `M` candidates by covariance-aware farthest-first profile distance. Materialize selected cotrees directly as adjacency matrices before converting them to triangular strings.

Every join adds all cross-module edges, every union adds none, and leaves contain no self-loops; consequently graph validity is guaranteed by construction for every legal `N`. Expected-gain check: nested join/union contacts are absent from every disjoint-clique-or-complement codeword, providing an evaluator-falsifiable new structural escape direction; keep this branch only if it scores above `17358828.78`.
